content:
Dear All,
I am a control theorist and I am new to both lean and open source contribution. I just wrote a few fundamental proofs for my area, motivated by chapter 3 of nonlinear control by hassan khalil.
Specifically, I have proven Gronwall-Bellman, the Comparison Lemma, and some Lyapunov stability results here: https://github.com/AnandGokhale/LeanForControl

I would like to know two things:
1) How would I proceed towards contributing this work to mathlib4's github
2) Would mathlib4 accept this kind of work?

I am happy to chat more

Hello!
Suggestion- I see you have some Gronwall stuff, can you go over Mathlib's existing file#Mathlib/Analysis/ODE/Gronwall and figure out what we're missing that you've proven, and contribute to that file?

Welcome!

  1. See leanprover-community.github.io/contribute
  2. Your code looks LLM-generated. We do not accept LLM-generated code from new contributors. If you rewrite the code significantly by hand, then we would be glad for you to open a PR, so long as you do not then use AI to address the review comments.

Thank you, yes, I am happy to contribute to that file, as I think I have proven a more general case than that file. My code is LLM-assisted for sure, as in, I gave an LLM an outline of a proof and then the LLM filled in my sorry's. I am actively working on simplifying it and making it easier to read, if that makes it acceptable.
Sadly if you do not learn Lean yourself, it does not
I am happy to do a significant rewrite to match the standards of mathlib4, and that will also force me to improve my understanding of lean in the process.
By rewrite you mean yourself manually, yes? Not asking an LLM to do that

Great! I advise you to create a PR sooner rather than later (but with human code), because reviews will help you adjust to Mathlib style of proofs and generalizations and API and all that. Also note that PRs on average contain less than 100 lines changed, so even just adding a lemma or two can be a great PR

Yes, I am planning to figure out what some easy results I can push are to learn the style. Like I said, I am new to open source, but I am very enthusiastic about what mathlib is building, and happy to contribute!
